---
title: "Syllabus"
---

## Learning Objectives

By the end of the course, students are expected to:

::: {.syllabus-grid}
::: {.syllabus-card}
#### Data Science Lifecycle
Understand the workflow from raw data to actionable insights.
:::

::: {.syllabus-card}
#### Modeling and Methods
Apply statistical and machine learning methods to structured datasets.
:::

::: {.syllabus-card}
#### Evaluation and Interpretation
Evaluate models and interpret results critically.
:::

::: {.syllabus-card}
#### Communication
Communicate findings clearly through reports and visualizations.
:::

::: {.syllabus-card}
#### Reproducibility
Build reproducible analysis pipelines.
:::
:::

## Topic Roadmap

The semester content is organized in five major blocks:

::: {.syllabus-grid .syllabus-grid-vertical}
::: {.syllabus-card}
#### Data Foundations
- Course introduction
- Data models
- Databases
- Data visualization
:::

::: {.syllabus-card}
#### Core Machine Learning
- Probability and statistics
- Regression
- Supervised learning
- Unsupervised and semi-supervised learning
- Causality
:::

::: {.syllabus-card}
#### Deep Learning
- Neural networks
- MLPs, feed-forward and recurrent networks
:::

::: {.syllabus-card}
#### Modern Architectures and Generative AI
- Transformers
- Small language model construction
- Generative models
- Diffusion models
- Time-series modeling with transformers
:::

::: {.syllabus-card}
#### ML Dataflow Engineering
- Data processing
- Model evaluation
- Model implementation
- Pipeline design
- Monitoring
:::
:::

For week-by-week sequencing and instructor assignment per session, refer to [Schedule](schedule.qmd).

## Prerequisites

::: {.policy-box}
- Programming experience (Python recommended)
- Basic probability and linear algebra
- Familiarity with calculus and introductory statistics
:::

## Grading Policy

::: {.policy-box}
- Assignments: 15%
- Project: 20%
- Quizzes: 15%
- Midterm: 20%
- Final Exam: 30%
:::

## Academic Integrity

::: {.policy-box}
Students must follow university academic integrity policies. Discussion is encouraged, but submitted work must be each student's own unless group work is explicitly allowed.
:::
